sections.h2: Installed sewage capacity covers 44% of generation; only about 28% is in use

chart.title: Capacity falls from 44% installed to about 28% actually utilised
chart.sub: Share of urban sewage generated (72,368 MLD), %.
chart.source: CPCB March 2021 inventory via PIB, 12 Dec 2022; Down To Earth.

sections.means: Of 72,368 MLD of urban sewage generated, 31,841 MLD is installed but only about 20,235 MLD is utilised.
sections.todo: CPCB should refresh its sewage treatment inventory, last comprehensively published in March 2021.

sections.h2: Namami Gange has 4,263 MLD complete, about 61% of its 7,000 MLD target

chart.title: Completed capacity rose from 3,806 to 4,263 MLD, still short of 7,000
chart.sub: Sewage treatment capacity, MLD, Namami Gange.
chart.source: PIB releases, Dec 2023 and Dec 2025; Lok Sabha reply, Aug 2026.

sections.means: Completed capacity grew from 3,806 MLD in October 2025 to 4,263 MLD in August 2026, against a 7,000 MLD target.
sections.todo: The National Mission for Clean Ganga should publish quarterly the status of the 1,625.50 MLD where construction has not started.

sections.h2: India's ~28% treatment share sits near lower-middle-income peers at 26%

chart.title: India tracks income peers, well below high-income countries at 74%
chart.source: UN-Water 2024 update and UN SDG 6 2025 report, via secondary reporting.

sections.means: India's roughly 28% is close to the lower-middle-income figure of 26%, while high-income countries reach 74%.
sections.todo: Judge India against income peers rather than the EU, as the post argues.
